messages:
maya: quick heads-up — starting a staged canary for release v3.2.1 in 5m (embed + routing fixes). i'll watch SLO dashboards p95/p99 and 5xx on embed-route. ping if you see anything.

sam: thanks — i'll be watching observability from my end. linking release notes: https://redwood.example/releases/v3.2.1 :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy started for service=embed-service env=prod stage=canary version=v3.2.1 target=10% traffic (rolling 2 hosts)

oliver: noted. quick checklist:
- p95 < 120ms baseline
- p99 < 300ms
- 5xx < 0.5% over 1m
- error budget no new spikes

ana: also watch KV cache hit ratio for canary — last patch touched cache eviction thresholds.

ops-bot: alert muted for noisy healthcheck-infra on /health (mute until +15m)

maya: sighted small p95 blip on embed-route at +2m, 3 hosts. p95 ~ 140ms, p99 stable. any correlates in traces?

sam: checking traces... looks like a tail latency issue on model-serialize step, a couple of traces show 250-300ms in serialize. not many 5xx.

oliver: metrics snapshot (5m window):
```
embed-route p95: 142ms (baseline 118ms)
embed-route p99: 298ms (baseline 290ms)
embed-route 5xx rate: 0.12%
kvcache hit: 91%
cpu util host-a: 68% host-b: 72% host-c: 70%
```

maya: that p95 delta is small but above our soft guard (120ms). i'm inclined to continue ramp but keep stricter watch. Thoughts on pin vs rollback?

sam: not a rollback yet. we can try pinning traffic to the two healthier hosts and reduce canary to 5% while we triage. command: `/pin-canary-hosts embed-service host-a,host-c --traffic=5%`

deploy-bot: received command: pin-canary-hosts embed-service hosts=[host-a,host-c] traffic=5%

ops-bot: done — traffic shifted, canary reduced to 5%. telemetry refresh in ~30s.

ana: after pin, p95 dropped to 125ms, p99 290ms. 5xx unchanged. KV hit steady. looks like host-b is the outlier.

oliver: agree. host-b processes show GC pause spikes at exactly the timeframe — digging into JVM GC logs now.

maya: good catch. sam, can we hold canary at 5% until GC fix or patch? if we proceed with full roll we'll risk higher client-visible latency.

sam: yes hold. i'm going to annotate release notes and changelog with known GC tail-latency risk and add a rollback runbook pointer.

maya: added comment to release notes: "observed GC tail latency on host-b during initial canary; hold at 5% until mitigated" https://redwood.example/releases/v3.2.1#notes

deploy-bot: canary hold acknowledged. automated rollback threshold still at 5xx >= 0.5% or p95 > 180ms for 3 consecutive minutes.

oliver: quick mitigation idea — bump Xmx on host-b before full rollout. will prepare a targeted patch and smoke it in staging.

sam: if all good in staging, we can schedule a controlled host-b restart with new JVM flags. prep a short downtime window for that host only.

maya: plan: hold canary @5% for now, oliver to push patch and test. if staging looks good, schedule host-b restart and then resume ramp. rollback only if 5xx crosses threshold.

ana: tagging SRE on-call FYI: @sam (you're on the ropes) :thumbsup:

sam: on it. posting final note here when we decide to resume.

deploy-bot: final state: canary=5% pinned hosts=[host-a,host-c], hold=true, monitor_rules active.

maya: thanks everyone — good fast triage. will update PMs and the release tracker. :white_check_mark:
